title: Summer Games II
build: US Gold's two-disk PAL release, as two G64 images: a BASIC boot file, a fast loader that stays at $0800-$0FFF, and fourteen packed modules read by one-letter names: the menu, the title, two ceremonies, eight events, and the first Summer Games' swimming events on side 2. Each part has its own listing

The event's entry: keeps the number of players less one in $7040, banks the ROMs out, copies the character sets into place, blanks the screen, clears $10 to $8F, writes FAULT into each player's result, starts the crowd, sets up the screen, the first frame, the sprites and the bar, starts the interrupt, draws the field and its colours, clears the status line and turns the screen on.
Waits for the interrupt to choose a new frame for the jumper, then unpacks it into the sprites.
Clears $10 to $8F, the event's variables.

Selects the VIC bank at $C000, the screen at $CC00 and the characters at $E000, sets the pacing variables, the tune, the jumper's place, state $9B and the bar at 1.50 m, chooses the first jumper and sets the sprite and screen colours.
Sets the border and background colours from $65CE.
The sprites' colours, read eight from here, so the last three come from the next table.
The border, background and two multicolour colours: black, dark grey, grey and white.
Waits for the frame, stops the CIA's timer interrupts, keeps the ROMs out, points the interrupt vector at $6609 and asks for line $FC.
Points the interrupt vector at $FFFE to irq.
The raster interrupt: steps down through three slots, sets the next line, and calls the slot's handler through the table at $6656, its low byte written into the operand at $6654.

The raster line set after each slot: $0A, $F0 and $91.

At the top of the screen sets the fine scroll from the run's position a frame late, places the sprites, picks the upper characters and colours, runs the state, works out the column and the bar, plays the tune or steps the sound effects, shows the screen drawn last and counts the frame.

Line $91, the field: waits a few cycles, picks the lower characters and the track's colours, allows interrupts and, when the column has changed, draws the screen not shown; otherwise copies the colours.
The lower part's background and multicolours: red, white and grey; the loop reads a fourth from the next byte.
Line $F0, the status line: a black background, the status font at $F000 and the screen at $C800, no fine scroll.

Reads the stick of the player's port.
Reads port X: when it has changed restarts a count of four frames and returns carry set; once it has held that long returns carry clear.
A routine nothing calls, which fills X pages from page Y, then a table of the rows' offsets, 40 apart, that nothing reads either.

Unpacks frame $3F into the five sprites not shown: each sprite's first byte is how many zero bytes end it, then the rest are copied in from the bottom up. Then shows that set and keeps where the frame's sprite offsets follow.
Finds which port's stick has moved, and remembers it.
Reads the player's stick, finding the port first; a new reading is kept in $1C and returns carry clear when it is lower, a press.
Turns the BCD byte in A into two screen digits, the tens in A and the units in X.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes.

Each state's handler: $7F next try, $81 a new try, $83 waiting for the stick, $85 finding the port, $87 the run, $89 the last strides, $8B the flight, $8D a good jump, $8F a failure, $91 and $93 waiting for the button, $95 waiting for the stick to be let go, $97 running past, $99 setting the bar, $9B the start, $9D pass or jump, $9F practice again.
The handlers from state $91 on.
State $9B: the tune, the music on, the sprites off, then a new try.
State $7F: goes on to a new try.
State $95: waits until the stick is let go.
State $9D: the height and < PASS  JUMP >; from 2.45 m on straight to the jump. Right jumps; left passes the height, marking the jumper, and moves on to the next.
State $81, a new try: the jumper's name, the start place, the run at its start and the flight cleared; then in a competition pass or jump, in practice the question.
State $9F: scrolls to the bar and, after the first jump, asks PRACTICE AGAIN?, any push turning YES and NO; the button on YES sets the bar, on NO goes back to the menu.
State $99: SET BAR HEIGHT. Up raises the bar by 0.05 m to at most 2.50, down lowers it to at least 1.20, and the button starts.
Goes to state $83, the run at its start.
State $83: the jumper fidgets, the attempt is shown, and a push of the stick starts the search for the port.
State $85: once the port is found, the empty tune, the sound effects on and the run.
Every 32 frames shows the next of frames 1 to 5, then waits 64 frames on frame 0.
State $87, the run: the stick steers and paces, the run moves on, and past $140 come the last strides.

Sets the speed to $0080, half a pixel a frame.
A press up or down moves the jumper's line by one, between $2D and $40; right adds a quarter of a pixel a frame to the speed, left halves it.
Moves the run on by the speed.
Returns carry clear once the run is past $140.
State $93: waits for the button, then goes back to the same try.
State $89, the last strides: the button takes off, when the jumper is in the take-off zone; otherwise running on. On a line above $30 or past $D0 a fault.
State $97: runs past the bar, slowing every eight frames, until past $D0 or stopped, then a fault.

State $8B, the flight: up held in the first five steps knocks the bar, and so does up let go in steps 8 to 10. A knocked bar falls from step 9. Each step lasts eight frames; at step 20 a good jump with the roar, or a failure.
State $8D: GOOD JUMP, the jumper marked clear, the crowd waving and the landing frames, then the result written.
State $8F: FAILED ATTEMPT, or ELIMINATED on the third, and the attempt counted.
State $91: waits for the button, then the next jumper.
